summary: The narrator takes a pink motorcycle from a rider on a gridlocked freeway at gunpoint, then rides back toward the Westside of Los Angeles during a citywide blackout and riot. Looters and rioters fill the streets, police are struggling to control the crowds, and the narrator kills a crowbar-wielding attacker who charges the bike. On reaching the apartment where Arthur was left, the narrator finds it dark and empty, and with no working cell phone has no way to contact him.
one_line: A narrator seizes a pink motorcycle during a Los Angeles blackout and riot, races back toward the Westside, and finds Arthur missing from the apartment.
key_facts: The narrator swung a Mossberg shotgun around and pointed it at the pink-clad biker to demand her bike.
The narrator threw the biker's pink-trimmed saddlebags at her and did not stop to steal her helmet.
The narrator rode the bike between two tractor-trailers and turned back toward LA, going the wrong way on the stopped freeway.
The 10 freeway was stopped all the way in, forcing the narrator onto the shoulder of an on ramp into gridlocked streets.
With no helmet on, the narrator could hear shouts and crashes and sirens from at least three directions.
The narrator describes Los Angeles as not famous for the cooperation of its residents in times of trouble, and says the looting had already started.
The city was black, with all the streetlights dead and silent and every building a blank, dark silhouette at night.
A hoodlum smashing car windows with a crowbar charged at the narrator's bike while hollering a wordless berserker cry.
The narrator released the clutch, rolled the throttle fully open, drew a handgun, and shot the hoodlum in the head.
The narrator was two streets away from the apartment where Arthur had been left.
The final block was lit by the pulsing red of police lights reflecting off pavement still wet from recent rain.
Officers with nightsticks were trying to corral belligerent rioters, and none of them paid any attention to the narrator.
The narrator burst into the flat and found it dark and empty, with Arthur not there.
With no working cell phone, the narrator had no way of contacting Arthur.
